knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(mgcv)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Item 1

```{r}
bikes <- read.csv("bikes.csv")
```


```{r}
ggplot(bikes, aes(x = hr, y = cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  labs(
    title = "Cantidad de bicicletas según la hora del día",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Cantidad de bicicletas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r}
promedio_hr <- bikes %>%
  group_by(hr) %>%
  summarise(cnt_promedio = mean(cnt))

ggplot(promedio_hr, aes(x = hr, y = cnt_promedio)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:23) +
  labs(
    title = "Promedio de bicicletas alquiladas por hora",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Promedio de bicicletas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```



```{r}
set.seed(123)

n <- nrow(bikes)

train <- sample(1:n, size = 0.7*n)

train_data <- bikes[train, ]
test_data  <- bikes[-train, ]
```




```{r}
modelo_lineal <- gam(cnt ~ hr, data = train_data)

pred <- predict(modelo_lineal, newdata = test_data)
```


```{r}
mse <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred)^2)

mse
```


```{r}
grid <- data.frame(hr = seq(0, 23, length.out = 200))
grid$pred <- predict(modelo_lineal, newdata = grid)

ggplot(test_data, aes(x = hr, y = cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(y = pred), color = "red", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Modelo lineal sobre el conjunto de test",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Cantidad de bicicletas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
Una recta no sirve porque la relación es no lineal...



# Item 2


```{r}
ks <- c(3, 6, 12, 24)


mse <- numeric(length(ks))
modelos <- vector("list", length(ks))

for(i in seq_along(ks)){

  modelos[[i]] <- gam(
    cnt ~ s(hr, k = ks[i], bs = "cr"),
    data = train_data
  )

  pred <- predict(modelos[[i]], newdata = test_data)

  mse[i] <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred)^2)
}

data.frame(k = ks, MSE = mse)
```


```{r}
grid <- data.frame(hr = seq(0, 23, length.out = 300))

predicciones <- lapply(seq_along(ks), function(i){

  data.frame(
    hr = grid$hr,
    pred = predict(modelos[[i]], newdata = grid),
    k = factor(ks[i])
  )

})

predicciones <- bind_rows(predicciones)
```


```{r}

ggplot(train_data, aes(hr, cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(
    data = predicciones,
    aes(y = pred, color = k),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Splines penalizados para distintos valores de k",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Cantidad de bicicletas",
    color = "k"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

A partir de 12 nodos se capturan los picos de demanda. Con k muy chico no se capturan estas tendencias.



# Item 3

```{r}
modelo_sp0 <- gam(
  cnt ~ s(hr, k = 24, bs = "cr", sp = 0),
  data = train_data
)

modelo_sp_grande <- gam(
  cnt ~ s(hr, k = 24, bs = "cr", sp = 1e4),
  data = train_data
)
```


```{r}
pred_sp0 <- predict(modelo_sp0, newdata = test_data)
pred_sp_grande <- predict(modelo_sp_grande, newdata = test_data)

mse_sp0 <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred_sp0)^2)
mse_sp_grande <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred_sp_grande)^2)

mse_sp0
mse_sp_grande
```


```{r}
summary(modelo_sp0)$s.table[, "edf"]

summary(modelo_sp_grande)$s.table[, "edf"]
```

```{r}
grid <- data.frame(hr = seq(0, 23, length.out = 300))

curvas <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    hr = grid$hr,
    pred = predict(modelo_sp0, newdata = grid),
    Modelo = "sp = 0"
  ),
  data.frame(
    hr = grid$hr,
    pred = predict(modelo_sp_grande, newdata = grid),
    Modelo = "sp = 1e4"
  )
)
```

```{r}
ggplot(train_data, aes(hr, cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(
    data = curvas,
    aes(y = pred, color = Modelo),
    linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Efecto del parámetro de penalización",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Cantidad de bicicletas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

El de sp = 0 "sobreajusta" ya que no hay penalización a la segunda derivada. Mientras que con sp=1e24 subajusta ya que la penalizacion es muy grande.



# Item 4


```{r}
modelo_gcv <- gam(
  cnt ~ s(hr, k = 24, bs = "cr"),
  data = train_data
)
```

```{r}
modelo_gcv$sp
```



```{r}
summary(modelo_gcv)$s.table[, "edf"]
```

```{r}
pred_gcv <- predict(modelo_gcv, newdata = test_data)

mse_gcv <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred_gcv)^2)

mse_gcv
```


```{r}
grid <- data.frame(hr = seq(0, 23, length.out = 300))
grid$pred <- predict(modelo_gcv, newdata = grid)

ggplot(train_data, aes(hr, cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = grid, aes(y = pred), color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  labs(
    title = "Spline penalizado con sp elegido por GCV",
    x = "Hora del día",
    y = "Cantidad de bicicletas"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

Parece haber encontrado un equilibrio...



# Item 5 


me aseguro que sea un factor

```{r}
train_data$mnth <- factor(train_data$mnth)
test_data$mnth <- factor(test_data$mnth)
```


y ahora ajusto el modelo

```{r}
modelo_re <- gam(
  cnt ~ s(hr, bs = "cr") + s(mnth, bs = "re"),
  data = train_data
)
```


```{r}
pred_re <- predict(modelo_re, newdata = test_data)

mse_re <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred_re)^2)

mse_re
```

mejora el mse

```{r}
coef_re <- coef(modelo_re)

coef_re[grep("mnth", names(coef_re))]
```

Un coeficiente positivo significa que ese mes hay una demanda mayor a la media, mientras que un coeficiente negativo hay menos demanda que la media.


# Item 6


Ajustamos el modelo Poisson


```{r}
modelo_pois <- gam(
  cnt ~ s(hr, bs = "cr") + s(mnth, bs = "re"),
  family = poisson(link = "log"),
  data = train_data
)
```



```{r}
pred_pois <- predict(modelo_pois,
                     newdata = test_data,
                     type = "response")

mse_pois <- mean((test_data$cnt - pred_pois)^2)

mse_pois
```

```{r}
grid <- data.frame(
  hr = seq(0, 23, length.out = 300),
  mnth = factor(6, levels = levels(train_data$mnth))
)

curvas <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    hr = grid$hr,
    pred = predict(modelo_re,
                   newdata = grid,
                   type = "response"),
    Modelo = "Gaussiano"
  ),
  data.frame(
    hr = grid$hr,
    pred = predict(modelo_pois,
                   newdata = grid,
                   type = "response"),
    Modelo = "Poisson"
  )
)

ggplot(train_data, aes(hr, cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(data = curvas,
            aes(y = pred, color = Modelo),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  theme_minimal()
```
